revisions.notes: Unchanged from last time: the dark-bezel green console sampled from the screenshots (#0a150e panel fill, #1d4227 hairline borders, #8ee39a ink, #c9ffd4 highlights, amber #e0b83a and red #e0554a states), square corners, tight monospace caps headers, left status rail, F1–F12 strip and the Status/mode chips across the top. This revision does two things only. (1) The radar port is now materially bigger: the situation-display column went from 1.3fr to 2fr (and 1.55fr of the height in the narrower two-row layout), the rail was slimmed to 142px, the right column to 244px, and panel padding around the scope tightened, so the scope keeps a near-square aspect while taking the largest area on the screen. (2) Panning: the scope slot now carries grab/grabbing cursors, touch-action:none, contained overscroll and no text selection so a press-and-drag on the picture is delivered to the live scope rather than to the page, with the offset-centre behaviour called out as fixed readouts in the scope footer and header ('drag to pan', 'OFFSET CENTRE OK'). While doing this I replaced the old hand-drawn zoom/scale button row — which had no wiring behind it — with the real data-slot="range" control in the same place, since a painted-but-dead scale switch is exactly the failure mode to avoid; the F1–F12 strip is retained as the reference's fixed page-index legend.

This revision keeps the earlier press-and-drag panning on the scope slot and now anchors the radar port so running interception messages cannot shrink it: the side columns are fixed pixel widths (rail 112px, tracks 300px, resources 216px), the main grid row is minmax(0,1fr), every panel body is overflow:hidden with its injected slot scrolling internally, and the decision slot has a fixed 78px height instead of a min-height \u2014 so the scope simply absorbs all remaining pixels. I also trimmed header/footer padding, the scope footer legend and rail label widths to give the scope more area. The F-key strip and the ID/fire keys are fixed lamps and labels, not pressable controls; the only real controls are the range and decision slots.
